subject: Fleet plan options for OrbitalCare — baseline ladder & ramp choices
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
To: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@orbitalcare.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 5 Nov 2025 09:17:00 -0800
Subject: Fleet plan options for OrbitalCare — baseline ladder & ramp choices

Hi Lena —

Following our demo and the usage profile you shared, attached is a concise set of deal-linked fleet options so you can pick the operational path that best matches your risk/cost profile. High level: we tailored three options (pilot -> grow -> anchored throughput) that map to typical product/ML stages.

Summary (short):
- Option A — Lean Pilot
  - Baseline: 20 GPUs reserved (min), warm pool enabled
  - Ramp: 2-week activation window, full capacity by day 14
  - Typical fit: small production pilot, bursty inference, cost-sensitive

- Option B — Growth Ladder (recommended for Q1 launch)
  - Baseline: 50 GPUs reserved (min) with 1:3 autoscale headroom
  - Ramp: phased activation over 6 weeks (10% increments every week)
  - Typical fit: steady production with predictable traffic growth, supports larger batch reranks and embedding pipelines

- Option C — Anchored Throughput
  - Baseline: 120 GPUs reserved (min) across 2 regions (primary + hot-failover)
  - Ramp: 16-week staged ramp (30/60/90/120 cadence), burst lanes for peak windows
  - Typical fit: latency-critical, enterprise SLAs, and heavy multi-model mixes

Tradeoffs and notes:
- Minimums are monthly committed minimums; you can configure burst credits to cover peak spikes.
- We recommend quantization & batching profile 1 for Options A/B to reduce cost while preserving quality; Option C can run mixed-precision profiles for throughput.
- Warmup credits: we include a one-time warmup token pool (equivalent to ~48 hours of steady traffic) with Option B and C.

Action items: please confirm the preferred option and the projected peak concurrent QPS + model mix (large gen vs. embedding vs. rerank). Once you pick, we’ll produce a short mutual action plan with activation milestones and an onboarding ETA.

Attachments: orbitalcare_fleet_plan_v1.xlsx (sizing spreadsheet), orbitalcare_terms_draft.pdf (term summary)

Thanks — happy to hop on a 30m call if you want to walk through the numbers.

—
Jordan Blake
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com
+1 (415) 555-0143

From: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@orbitalcare.ai>

Cc: Victor Huang <victor.huang@orbitalcare.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 5 Nov 2025 11:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Fleet plan options for OrbitalCare — baseline ladder & ramp choices

Thanks Jordan — this is helpful. A couple of clarifying questions before we pick: 

1) For Option B (Growth Ladder) can you explain what you mean by "1:3 autoscale headroom" — does that require additional committed GPUs or is that on top of the 50 GPU baseline?
2) How do warmup credits get consumed? Will we see them as a line item on monthly usage?
3) Do any of these options require traffic to route through Redwood's hosted control plane for metrics/rollouts, or can we keep a private plane (OrbitalCare VPC) and still take advantage of warmup and quantization profiles?
4) Pricing: do you have a rough 12-month blended unit cost for Option B vs Option C?

Also, security team asks: will Redwood provide an ingress IP allowlist for dedicated capacity? They want the audit log retention details for the first 90 days.

If it helps, our target is to start a limited production launch in January. Our primary model mix at launch will be: 60% medium-gen, 25% embeddings, 15% rerank/quality checks. Peak concurrent requests estimated ~420 QPS (p95 payloads).

Can we get a redlineable mutual action plan and a sketch of the onboarding timeline?

Best,
Lena Ortiz
Head of Product, OrbitalCare
lena.ortiz@orbitalcare.ai

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
To: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@orbitalcare.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 5 Nov 2025 14:28:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Fleet plan options for OrbitalCare — baseline ladder & ramp choices

Lena — great questions, answered inline below.

On Tue, 5 Nov 2025 at 11:03 AM Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@orbitalcare.ai> wrote:
> 1) For Option B (Growth Ladder) can you explain what you mean by "1:3 autoscale headroom" — does that require additional committed GPUs or is that on top of the 50 GPU baseline?

Good question. The 50 GPUs is the reserved baseline (monthly commit). The 1:3 headroom is our autoscaling policy for live traffic that allows up to 150 GPUs to be spun up transiently (on-demand) subject to availability and burst credits. That headroom is not part of the committed minimum; it is billed as usage when consumed. We can optionally convert part of that headroom into a soft-reserved buffer if you want a guaranteed floor above 50.

> 2) How do warmup credits get consumed? Will we see them as a line item on monthly usage?

Warmup credits are consumed during the initial activation period and any large model warmstarts. They are shown as a separate line on the invoice as a credit item for the month the activation occurs.

> 3) Do any of these options require traffic to route through Redwood's hosted control plane for metrics/rollouts, or can we keep a private plane (OrbitalCare VPC) and still take advantage of warmup and quantization profiles?

You can keep a private control plane (VPC Private deployment) and still get the optimization features. For warmup we coordinate via a short signed webhook handshake; nothing about inference payloads leaves your VPC unless you choose hosted telemetry. Audit logs and retention are available in both modes — we'll provide the 90-day retention export for your security team.

> 4) Pricing: do you have a rough 12-month blended unit cost for Option B vs Option C?

Attached spreadsheet (orbitalcare_fleet_plan_v1.xlsx) has model-by-model cost curves. High level: Option B blended token cost is estimated 28% lower than the pilot per-unit number due to batching/quantization gains; Option C drives another ~12% improvement at scale. I dropped a 12-month blended example in the sheet; we can switch assumptions if you prefer a more conservative traffic curve.

Next steps / mutual action plan sketch:
- You confirm preferred option + initial model mix (you already gave a good start) — by EOD Nov 10
- Redwood drafts a short MOU + onboarding milestones (networking, keys, canary tests) — 48 hours after confirmation
- Activation window: Option B timeline sets onboarding kickoff two weeks after MOU and staged activation over 6 weeks; engineering ramp gate at week 3 (canary traffic 10-40%)

Security notes: we will provide an ingress IP allowlist for dedicated nodes and a machine-readable audit log export (90-day retention) for the enterprise package.

I pasted the HubSpot link to the draft plan here: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/6829 and uploaded the sheet to the shared drive (link above).

If you'd like, I can schedule a 30m call Thursday to walk the numbers with your infra/security leads.

—
Jordan Blake
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwoodinference.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 12 Nov 2025 15:42:00 -08:00
Subject: Fwd: Fleet plan options for OrbitalCare — pricing tweak request

Grace / Jordan — forwarding the thread. OrbitalCare liked Option B but pushed back on the 50 GPU baseline; they're asking if we can tighten the minimum to 40 GPUs if we provide a 10% onboarding credit for the first 3 months. That would improve their cashflow without changing the ramp timing.

Proposed commercial tweak (internal):
- Adjust Option B baseline to 40 GPUs committed
- Maintain 1:3 autoscale headroom (so transient capacity still reaches 120)
- Offer 10% credit on committed spend for months 1–3 (warmup credit separate)

If Grace approves, I’ll route a short amendment to the terms draft and loop OrbitalCare. Thoughts?

—
Ben Carter
Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference
